pr_body:
Also EVP_KEY_new_CMAC_key_ex which was in the pre-release 3.0

Fixes: #13628

----
EVP_KEY_new_CMAC_key_ex was added in an earlier alpha release, and documented, so this PR just removes it and makes it undocumented. That might be controversial, but it doesn't make sense to document a function and deprecate it all in the same release.

Note that this takes the same approach as Pauli's #13652 PR, the functions are deprecated but existing code isn't rewritten.

issue_context.title: Deprecate EVP_PKEY_new_CMAC_key_ex() and EVP_PKEY_new_CMAC_key() ?
issue_context.body: Considering that we discourage doing MAC via EVP_PKEY, it only seems fitting to discourage the use of these functions.
comments: I'm willing to make a PR for this if it should happen for 3.0 (which seems like yes, but confirmation would be appreciated).
You got it, thanks for offering
Note that ```EVP_PKEY_new_CMAC_key_ex``` was added in 3.0 so it can just be removed.

I had forgotten about this and am just now getting back to it.

What function replaces ```EVP_PKEY_NEW_CMAC_key```? Since that function takes a ```EVP_CIPHER*``` parameter, I'm not sure what you were thinking should be done here, @levitte?

> I had forgotten about this and am just now getting back to it.
> 
> What function replaces `EVP_PKEY_NEW_CMAC_key`? Since that function takes a `EVP_CIPHER*` parameter, I'm not sure what you were thinking should be done here, @levitte?

You just would not use the EVP_PKEY interface for handling CMAC and HMAC at all and use EVP_MAC API instead. You would just set the OSSL_MAC_PARAM_CIPHER param on the EVP_MAC_CTX.
Deprecation (and removal) done now on master with #13829
